messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: DI-water batch tests are clearly described (20 mL DI water, 1 g/L adsorbent, 10 mg/L of each contaminant, 24 h, 24±2 °C, 200 rpm), and the same core conditions are used for groundwater and wastewater matrix tests (1 g/L adsorbent, 24 h contact time, same PFAS concentration range). It is reasonable to treat the DI-water batch tests as a clean-water baseline that is comparable with conditions to other matrices.

The methods explicitly describe adsorption experiments and determination of the quantity adsorbed from the difference between initial and final concentrations, which corresponds to a sorption endpoint (adsorption efficiency, isotherms).
The abstract states that adsorption followed the order PFOS > PFOA > GenX and that Cd(II) enhanced or inhibited adsorption of PFAS, clearly indicating a sorption endpoint.

The source notes that adsorption isotherms in different matrices were generated with a limited number of data points, but it does not explicitly state that this may affect precision of fitted parameters; that consequence is inferred by the extractor.
Bench-scale batch tests in DI water are clearly described, and noting that such controlled conditions may not capture all complexities of natural waters is a reasonable design-inferred limitation.

The batch experiments are described as using 20 mL deionized water spiked with a mixture of PFAS and Cd(II), and all laboratory solutions prepared with DI water (Elga PURELAB Chorus, 18.2 MΩ·cm). However, the value also labels the matrix as “Milli-Q,” which is used elsewhere in the paper for PFAS-spiked Milli-Q water but is not stated for this specific DI batch setup, so part of the descriptor is not directly supported.
Batch experiments were conducted in 50-mL amber glass bottles and the bottles were sealed during shaking, matching the described reactor configuration.
No unit is appropriate for a descriptive reactor-configuration field; unit is correctly null.
Each bottle contained 20 mL of deionized water, matching the solution volume value of 20.
The volume is expressed in mL in the text, consistent with the recorded unit.
Each bottle had 20 mg adsorbent in 20 mL solution, explicitly stated as 1 g L−1; the numeric value of 1 matches this dose.
The dose is reported as 1 g L−1, consistent with the recorded unit g/L.
The mixture of PFAS and Cd(II) had an initial concentration of 10 mg L−1 of each contaminant, so 10 mg/L per PFAS is supported.
Concentrations are explicitly given in mg L−1, matching the mg/L unit.
Cd(II) is included in the mixture at an initial concentration of 10 mg L−1 of each contaminant, supporting the value of 10.
The unit mg/L matches the reported 10 mg L−1 concentration for Cd(II).
The batch experiments were run for 24 h, supporting a contact time value of 24.
The duration is stated in hours; unit h is correct.
The sealed bottles were shaken at 200 rpm on a platform shaker, matching the agitation value of 200.
Shaking speed is expressed in rpm in the source, consistent with the unit rpm.
The experiments were conducted at 24 ± 2 °C; the recorded value “24 ± 2” matches this description.
Temperature is reported in °C in the source, consistent with the unit.
All laboratory solutions were prepared using deionized water (Elga PURELAB Chorus, 18.2 MΩ·cm), supporting the background water type description.
The field is descriptive of water type; a null unit is appropriate.
Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) is listed among the target PFAS used in the study.
Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is listed among the target PFAS used in the study.
Perfluoro-2-propoxypropanoic acid (GenX) is listed among the target PFAS and identified by name and acronym.
The batch setup uses 20 mg adsorbent in 20 mL solution, explicitly 1 g L−1; the numeric value of 1 is correct for adsorbent dose.
Adsorbent dose is reported as 1 g L−1 in the source, matching the g/L unit.
The mixture of PFAS and Cd(II) has 10 mg L−1 of each contaminant; thus an initial PFOA concentration of 10 mg/L is supported.
The concentration unit mg/L matches the reported mg L−1 for each contaminant.
PFOS is part of the mixture at 10 mg L−1 of each contaminant, supporting the value 10 mg/L.
The unit mg/L is consistent with the source’s mg L−1 notation.
GenX is one of the contaminants in the mixture at 10 mg L−1 of each contaminant, so 10 mg/L is supported.
The source uses mg L−1 for these concentrations, consistent with mg/L.
Cd(II) is included in the mixture at an initial concentration of 10 mg L−1 of each contaminant, supporting the value 10 mg/L.
The unit mg/L matches the reported mg L−1 for Cd(II).
Experiments are described as batch adsorption tests in 50-mL amber glass bottles with defined lab conditions, clearly indicating bench-scale batch adsorption in a DI water matrix.

The methods describe adsorption onto commercial activated carbon and three biochars (BC-W, BC-SS550, BC-SS700), and later text notes that AC and BC-W were selected for further evaluation due to superior performance, consistent with the treatment description.

result.record_usable_rationale: Core elements—source identity, DI-water matrix with PFAS + Cd(II), adsorption treatment materials, sorption endpoints, operating conditions, and quantitative concentrations/doses—are directly supported by the cited text. Minor issues (e.g., inclusion of “Milli-Q” in the DI matrix description and an inferred impact of limited data points on isotherm precision) are qualifier-level and do not compromise interpretability of the main experimental conditions or findings.
